issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
The infra nightly matrix reduces every observed run to healthy or unhealthy. Although the GitHub bridge reads the run's `queued`, `in_progress`, or `completed` status, `/github/nightlies` does not return it. A queued or in-progress run is therefore rendered as a red failure until it completes.

The header compounds this by reporting only `healthy / due`, which groups running, failed, missing-run, and unavailable states together. The legend does not define running or unavailable, and `missing` does not tell a new viewer that GitHub created no run.

This was visible on August 31 when [Datakit tier 2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33405458686) was in progress but appeared failed, while overdue schedules with no GitHub run appeared in the separate dark-red missing state.

Expected behavior:

- Show queued and in-progress runs as blue `Running`, with elapsed time.
- Show an overdue schedule with no observed GitHub run as `No run`.
- Keep completed success green, completed or quality-gate failure red, slow success amber, datasource unavailable orange, and not-yet-due neutral.
- Pair every color with a distinct icon and plain label, and explain every state in the legend and tooltip.
- Replace the healthy ratio with categorical counts such as `3 passed · 1 running · 4 no run · 2 failed`.

Do not change cron schedules, grace periods, or nightly quality gates. This issue only makes the dashboard report its existing observations clearly.

cc @rjpower

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## Description
Generalize the paged-attention execution config introduced in #6099 from `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` to a backend-neutral `PagedAttentionConfig` draccus choice family.

The current config combines backend selection with TPU-specific tuning fields. That is already awkward for `tpu-inference` versus JAX RPA, and it will get worse once a GPU implementation lands. Keep the policy passed through decode, but make the config type generic and dispatch by concrete choice type rather than a TPU-only enum.

Suggested choices: `auto`, `reference`, `tpu-inference`, `jax-rpa`, and later a GPU backend choice.

### Definition of Done
- `decode` and attention call sites accept `PagedAttentionConfig`, not `TpuPagedAttentionConfig`.
- TPU-specific tunables live only on TPU-specific choice dataclasses.
- `paged_attention_with_kv_update` dispatches by config choice type.
- Existing TPU paged-attention tests cover the renamed/generic config surface.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and AGENTS / fix-issue / author-pr skills
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (PR #6099, related issues)
- [x] Inspect `TpuPagedAttentionConfig`, dispatch, and call sites on the #6099 branch
- [x] Decide on PR vs analysis: posting analysis (depends on #6099; design change spans 5+ files)

**Research**

The code this issue refers to lives only on the open draft [PR #6099](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6099) (`codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention`); nothing matching `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` / `paged_attention_with_kv_update` is on `main` yet. The current `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` mixes three concerns: backend selection (generic), dispatch policy (`allow_autotune`, `fail_on_reference_fallback` — generic), and backend-specific tunables (`tpu_inference_out_dtype`, `preserve_attention_output_dtype` for tpu-inference; `num_kv_pages_per_block`, `num_queries_per_block`, `vmem_limit_bytes` for JAX RPA). Dispatch is a string-enum if/elif chain in `_run_backend`, so adding a GPU backend later means widening every model signature and growing the enum/branch list.

Relevant code (PR #6099 branch):
- [`tpu_kernels.py#L22-L41`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/tpu_kernels.py#L22-L41) — `TpuPagedAttentionBackend` enum + `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` dataclass.
- [`tpu_kernels.py#L301-L396`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/tpu_kernels.py#L301-L396) — `_run_backend` / `paged_attention_with_kv_update` enum dispatch and fallback chain.
- [`attention.py#L1777`, `#L1961`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L1777) — call sites in `PagedKvCacheAttention.decode` variants.
- [`llama.py#L357`, `#L431`, `#L641`, `#L685`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/llama.py#L357) and [`apertus.py#L301`, `#L363`, `#L484`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/apertus.py#L301) — model decode signatures.
- [`test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/tests/inference/test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py), [`test_qwen3.py#L18`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/tests/test_qwen3.py#L18) — tests that construct the config.

**Proposed Approach (for review before implementing)**

Treat this as a design change to land **after** #6099 merges; opening a parallel PR off the draft branch would conflict. Suggested shape:

1. New module `lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/paged_attention_config.py`:
   - Abstract base `PagedAttentionConfig` registered with draccus as a choice family.
   - Generic policy fields on the base: `fail_on_reference_fallback: bool`, plus multi-backend ordering handled via a wrapper like `AutoPagedAttentionConfig(candidates=...)` rather than a magic `AUTO` enum value.
   - Concrete choices: `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig`, `JaxRpaPagedAttentionConfig` (holds `num_kv_pages_per_block`, `num_queries_per_block`, `vmem_limit_bytes`), `TpuInferencePagedAttentionConfig` (holds `out_dtype`, `preserve_attention_output_dtype`, `vmem_limit_bytes`), and later `GpuPagedAttentionConfig`.
   - Each choice exposes a `run(q, new_k, new_v, kv_cache, batch_info, *, sm_scale, soft_cap) -> tuple[NamedArray, KvPageCache]` method; `paged_attention_with_kv_update` becomes a thin entry point that walks the candidate list, catches `UnsupportedPagedAttentionBackend`, and emits a fallback warning. No `if/elif backend == ...` chain remains.

2. Rename the `tpu_paged_attention` parameter on `PagedKvCacheAttention.decode`, `LlamaDecoderLayer.decode`, `LlamaTransformer.decode`, `LlamaLMHeadModel.decode`, and the Apertus equivalents to `paged_attention: PagedAttentionConfig`. Default to `AutoPagedAttentionConfig()`.

3. Keep `TpuPagedAttentionShape` and platform/shape gating helpers, but move them into the TPU-specific choice classes (they call `tpu_paged_attention_supports_shape` internally). No backward-compat shim per AGENTS.md "NO BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY".

4. Update `test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py` and `test_qwen3.py` to construct concrete choices (`JaxRpaPagedAttentionConfig()`, `TpuInferencePagedAttentionConfig()`, `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig()`) and parameterize on those directly instead of the string enum.

5. Estimated diff: ~400-600 lines across `tpu_kernels.py` (split into `paged_attention_config.py` + `tpu_pallas_backend.py`), `tpu_inference_adapter.py` (no signature change), `attention.py`, `llama.py`, `apertus.py`, two test files. Above the <100 LOC PR threshold, hence this design comment instead of a direct PR.

**Open questions for the issue author**

- Should the choice family base live in `levanter.inference` (next to backends) or in `levanter.layers.attention` (next to the call sites)?
- Is `AutoPagedAttentionConfig(candidates=[...])` the preferred way to express the current `AUTO` policy, or do you want a top-level `auto` choice that internally re-resolves to a platform-derived default each call?
- Confirm the `fail_on_reference_fallback` semantics belong on the base config rather than only on `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig` — keeping it on the base preserves today's "I picked tpu-inference and refuse to silently fall back to reference" behaviour.

Will wait for confirmation on #6099 merging and the questions above before opening a PR.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
🤖
## Description
Add target-only PPL eval slices for low-level text and interpreter mechanics. The eval should cover exact token-to-character decomposition across every Marin tokenizer id that is representable in normal UTF-8 text, report byte-fallback/replacement-character ids that cannot round-trip through JSONL text, and include small circuit-style probes for character counts, indices, line lengths, indentation, arithmetic, and Python REPL surfaces.

### Definition of Done
- Generate eval-only JSONL records with `input`, `target`, and provenance metadata.
- Verify every representable non-special Marin tokenizer id included in vocab coverage appears in at least one rendered input as that token id.
- Emit a coverage summary for excluded ids that cannot be exposed as normal Unicode text.
- Register the bundle in the perplexity-gap registry for Marin 32B vs Qwen3 32B scoring.
- Add focused tests for tokenizer coverage verification, target-only rendering, metadata/tags, and local JSONL staging.
- Provide the dry-run/run command for the scoring job and record the output artifact paths when run.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and check actionability
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Survey existing eval-slice pattern and registry
- [x] Post Research + Proposed Approach for human review
- [ ] Await design confirmation before implementation (scope exceeds the 100-line PR threshold for agent-authored fixes)

# Research

Issue asks for a new target-only PPL bundle covering tokenizer/interpreter mechanics (char counts, indices, line lengths, indentation, arithmetic, Python REPL) plus a vocab-coverage invariant over the Marin tokenizer, and registration in the perplexity-gap registry against the existing \`marin_32b\` vs \`qwen3_32b\` pair. No existing slice covers this — the closest analogs are the identifier-encoding and delimiter-format families.

Definition of done is concrete, but two design choices need a human decision before code lands: (a) storage surface for the bundle, and (b) what \"every non-special token id appears\" means in practice given the ~100k Marin vocab.

**Relevant code**
- [\`experiments/evals/synthetic_identifier_encoding_ppl.py\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/synthetic_identifier_encoding_ppl.py) — template for slice family + JSONL writer + sample harness
- [\`experiments/evals/synthetic_delimiter_format_ppl.py#L385-L411\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/synthetic_delimiter_format_ppl.py#L385-L411) — alternative pattern using local \`StepSpec\` materialization (no HF push)
- [\`experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L113-L183\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L113-L183) — bundle factories, \`registered_perplexity_gap_bundles\`, and the \`marin_32b\` / \`qwen3_32b\` pair already exist
- [\`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L116-L142\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L116-L142) — \`supervised_text_dataset\` is the target-only entry point
- [\`experiments/exp_model_perplexity_gap_coverage_matrix.py\`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/exp_model_perplexity_gap_coverage_matrix.py) — dry-run / run command; new bundle is picked up automatically once registered

# Proposed Approach

New module \`experiments/evals/circuit_coverage_ppl.py\` modeled on \`synthetic_identifier_encoding_ppl.py\`:

1. \`CircuitCoverageFamily(StrEnum)\` with six task families: \`vocab_coverage\`, \`char_counts\`, \`char_indices\`, \`line_lengths\`, \`indentation\`, \`arithmetic\`, \`python_repl\`. One \`CircuitCoveragePplSlice\` per family with tags \`loss:target_only\`, \`epic:5005\`, \`issue:6103\`, \`source:generated_circuit_coverage_ppl_v1\`, seed/examples, family/task.
2. Deterministic row generator (RNG seeded per row, same \`seed + slice_offset + row_index\` pattern) producing \`{input, target, id, subset, task, seed, metadata}\` JSONL records. Each family is small and probe-style:
   - \`char_counts\`: \"How many 'x' in 'abxxcx'? Answer: \" → \`3\\n\`
   - \`char_indices\`: \"The 4th char of 'abcdef' is \" → \`d\\n\`
   - \`line_lengths\`: \"Line length of 'foo bar baz': \" → \`11\\n\`
   - \`indentation\`: snippets with 2/4/8-space and tab leading prefixes; predict the continuation indent
   - \`arithmetic\`: small base-10 add/sub/mul, target is digits-only continuation
   - \`python_repl\`: short \`>>> expr\\n\` interactions where target is the next \`>>> \` line or the result
   - \`vocab_coverage\`: see below
3. **Vocab-coverage invariant**: load \`marin-community/marin-tokenizer\` once, enumerate \`{id: token}\` excluding \`all_special_ids\` and any \`added_tokens_decoder\` entries marked special. For each non-special id, emit a row whose rendered \`input + target\` re-tokenizes to a sequence containing that id at least once. Cheapest construction: \`tokenizer.decode([id])\` round-tripped through a fixed framing prompt (e.g. \`\"Token: \" + decoded + \"\\n\"\`), then verified by re-encoding under \`add_special_tokens=False\`. Rows where the round-trip drops the id (mojibake / merge boundary issues) get a fallback construction that places the decoded fragment between two known-stable anchor strings until the id reappears; if no construction works after N attempts, raise (fail fast — invariant must be true by construction, not by chance).
4. Tests in new \`tests/evals/test_circuit_coverage_ppl.py\`:
   - Tokenizer coverage: load tokenizer, generate \`vocab_coverage\` slice, assert \`{id} ⊆ tokens(input+target for every row)\` covers \`vocab − special_ids\`. Real tokenizer, no mocks.
   - Target-only rendering: every row has non-empty \`input\` and \`target\`; both keys round-trip through \`supervised_text_dataset\` and produce a \`RawTextEvaluationDataset\` with \`input_key=\"input\"\`, \`target_key=\"target\"\`.
   - Metadata/tags: each slice's \`tags\` tuple contains the required tags; \`metadata\` carries \`family\` and probe-specific keys.
   - Local JSONL staging: \`write_circuit_coverage_jsonl_configs(tmp_path)\` produces one file per slice, each line valid JSON with the required schema.
5. Registry: add \`circuit_coverage_bundle()\` in \`experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py\` and append it to \`registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()\`. The existing \`PerplexityGapPair(\"marin_32b\", \"qwen3_32b\")\` then picks it up automatically.
6. Scoring command (no new entry point needed):
   \`uv run python experiments/exp_model_perplexity_gap_coverage_matrix.py --dry_run\` for dry-run, drop \`--dry_run\` for the real run. Artifact paths land under \`analysis/model_perplexity_scores/circuit_coverage/{marin_32b,qwen3_32b}\` and \`analysis/perplexity_gap/circuit_coverage/marin_32b-vs-qwen3_32b\`.

# Open questions for the issue author

1. **Storage surface**: HF-hosted (like \`marin-community/synth-identifier-encoding-ppl\`) or local-only via \`StepSpec\` materialization (like \`synthetic_delimiter_format_ppl\`)? The latter avoids a new HF dataset repo and revision pin.
2. **Vocab-coverage size**: Marin tokenizer is ~100k tokens. One row per non-special id ≈ 100k rows for that slice alone. OK as the spec reads, but should we cap at a stratified sample (e.g. all unique tokens by frequency decile) to keep the bundle within \`max_docs_per_dataset=256\`? If kept at full coverage, the bundle needs a per-slice \`max_docs_per_dataset\` override.
3. **Python REPL surface**: scope to single-line \`>>> expr\` continuations, or include multi-line tracebacks / \`...\` continuations?

Implementation is straightforward and well-scoped once (1)-(3) are decided. Happy to proceed once confirmed.

issues.title: Hero Run Checkpoint Prompt Completions

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
## TL;DR

The final Hero forecast is 0.7406 Paloma BPB. Nemotron 3 Super-120B-A12B-Base measures 0.7918 BPB, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base measures 0.8397 BPB, and Nemotron 3 Nano-30B-A3B-Base measures 0.8846 BPB. The Hero forecast is 6.5% lower than Super, 11.8% lower than Qwen, and 16.3% lower than Nano. It is lower than Super on 14 of 16 Paloma subsets.

![Hero and three open-weight models by Paloma subset](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/paloma-subset-forecasts.png)

## Description

Compare Hero with open-weight base models on the same evaluation data. Report bits per byte (BPB) because token perplexity is not comparable across tokenizers.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure each base model with the Hero evaluation protocol. Add each result to the same comparison.

## Status

| Model | Paloma BPB | UncheatableEval BPB |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hero final forecast | 0.7406 | — |
| Nemotron 3 Super-120B-A12B-Base | 0.7918 | 0.4964 |
| Hero without token dropping, step 45,837 | 0.8188 | 0.5362 |
| Hero with token dropping, step 45,837 | 0.8868 | 0.6220 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base | 0.8397 | 0.5245 |
| Nemotron 3 Nano-30B-A3B-Base | 0.8846 | 0.5703 |

Nano and Super use the full 15-subset UncheatableEval. The Hero and Qwen values use the earlier 7-subset suite, so those UncheatableEval values are not directly comparable with Nano and Super.

Each subset forecast fits BPB as a function of Paloma macro-loss across 77 paired ladder measurements. It then applies the preregistered macro-loss scaling law. Fifteen fits have `R² ≥ 0.997`; Twitter AAE has `R² = 0.971`.

The Hero forecast is 6.6% to 21.6% lower than Qwen and 8.0% to 38.5% lower than Nano across the 16 subsets. It is 1.0% to 40.3% lower than Super on 14 subsets. Super is 5.1% lower on M2D2 Wikipedia and 9.2% lower on WikiText-103.

The FLOP axis uses `6 × active parameters × training tokens` estimates. Super is at `1.8e24` FLOPs from 12B active parameters and 25T tokens. NVIDIA reports over 25T tokens, so this is a lower-bound coordinate. Qwen is at `6.48e23` FLOPs from 3B active parameters and a 36T-token assumption. Nano is at `5.25e23` FLOPs from NVIDIA's published 3.5B active parameters and 25T training tokens. Exact FLOP totals for the hybrid MoE architectures are unknown.

A bootstrap over the four ladder runs gives 0.7404–0.7432 macro BPB. This range covers the loss-to-BPB conversion. It does not cover error in the loss forecast.

The forecast assumes a 4K context, the original data mix, and the planned token count. These inputs can change before training ends. We do not have a final UncheatableEval forecast.

## Links

- [Interactive report and plots](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/index.html)
- [Subset forecast data](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/paloma-subset-forecast-analysis.json)
- [Macro forecast data](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/hero-bpb-forecast-analysis.json)
- [Evaluation data](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/metrics.json)
- [Scaling-ladder code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d23e6e9c3673435fb82d83aa6c51a607d0da6009/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/plot_scaling_ladder.py)
- [Hero run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-12d8b6f0-dee637)
- [Qwen result](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/qwen-results.json)
- [Nano result](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/nemotron-nano-results.json)
- [Super result](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.08.31.4/nemotron-super-results.json)
- [Nano Evaldash run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/20260901-040435-nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b-base-paloma-uncheatable-c989)
- [Super Evaldash run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/20260901-045340-nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b-base-paloma-uncheatable-9329)
- [Qwen model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base)
- [Nano model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Base-BF16)
- [Super model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-Base-BF16)

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-31: Use BPB for comparisons across tokenizers.
- 2026-08-31: Limit the final forecast to Paloma. UncheatableEval has no final forecast.
- 2026-09-01: Place Qwen, Nano, and Super on the FLOP axis with labeled 6ND estimates. Super's coordinate is a lower bound because NVIDIA reports over 25T training tokens.

## Conclusion

Qwen, Nano, and Super are complete under the same evaluation protocol.

## Human Authored tl;dr

WHAT THIS IS: In this experiment, we started with a Qwen3 Coder model and a moderately challenging RL dataset from TaskTrove and asked the question whether DAPO or GSPO would outperform GRPO in producing stable reward curves.

WHY WE DID IT: We still do not have a reliable learning formula for agentic RL when the data is highly heterogeneous and challenging (e.g., SWE-Smith); ideally, this experiment would provide such a starting point.

RESULT: The experiment was entirely inconclusive.
* JSC Jupiter underwent a series of severe hardware failures which confounded the results
* The dataset initially selected for the study had quality issues and needed a version update mid-experiment
* The DAPO objective prevented reward collapse but introduced a new failure mode of starvation; 70%+ of groups produced no advantage and were discarded

### Helpful links

- Full campaign artifact archive (configs, curves, analyses, cleanup logs): https://huggingface.co/datasets/penfever/jupiter-tasktrove-dapo-artifacts
- Operating policy (second post below): https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8829#issuecomment-5492609149

comments.body:
# POLICY — Jupiter TaskTrove DAPO

Durable operating rules. Chronology, run IDs, measurements, incidents, and blockers belong in
`STATE.md`, never here.

Derived from `experiments/complete/tasktrove-hparam-optimization/POLICY.md` (owner instruction,
2026-08-20). Rules carried over unchanged are not re-justified here; rules that CHANGED for this
campaign are marked **[CHANGED]** with the reason.

## Scope

- Base model is `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct`, unchanged from the predecessor campaigns.
- Agent harness is **terminus-2**.
- **[CHANGED] The RL dataset is `laion/codeforces-v2`**, not TaskTrove `DCAgent/exp_rpt_multifile`.
  It ships a single root-level `tasks.parquet` rather than the TaskTrove `<subdir>/tasks.parquet`
  layout; confirm the extraction resolves it before trusting a launch.
- **[CHANGED] The objective is DAPO**, not RLOO-N. DAPO here means GRPO group advantages with
  decoupled clipping (`eps_clip_low` 0.2 / `eps_clip_high` 0.4), token-level loss
  (`loss_reduction: token_mean`), and dynamic sampling (`type: filter`).
- The swept variable is the objective's own settings. Hold geometry, harness and context budget
  fixed so objective changes stay attributable.

## Dataset eligibility

`laion/codeforces-v2` is admitted by owner instruction, not by the predecessor's four-rule screen.
Two of those rules still bind as **read gates rather than admission gates**, because they can only
be evaluated once the arm runs:

1. **Difficulty band.** Reject the source if step-1 `reward/avg_pass_at_8` pins near 1.0000, or if
   most groups are uniform-zero. Under DAPO both failures present the same way — dynamic sampling
   discards nearly every group — so read the raw pass@8 before concluding anything about training.
2. **Verifier integrity.** Collapsed reward with empty transcripts or widespread verifier
   exceptions is stop-and-debug, not a data-quality verdict.

Record the verdict and its evidence in `TRACKER.md` before launching a second arm.

## DAPO-specific rules **[CHANGED — new section]**

- **`max_sample_batches` is capped at 3 and may not be raised without owner authorization.** A
  discarded group on an agentic source costs a full wave of sandboxed terminus-2 episodes, not a
  batch of text completions. At 8 (the snowball E11 value) one step can consume the entire 11:59
  window without banking a checkpoint.
- If the filter repeatedly hits the cap, the response is to lower `n_samples_per_prompt` or to
  question DAPO on agentic rollouts. Raising the cap is not a remedy.
- `eps_clip_high` 0.4 is the entropy risk in this configuration. Lower it toward the DAPO paper's
  0.28 before touching any other lever if entropy climbs.
- Do not carry `use_kl_loss: false` forward as a silent default if a KL arm is later added.

## Training configuration

- Runs on **Jupiter (JSC)**, not Iris, through `python -m hpc.launch --job_type rl`.
- Geometry is fixed at 6 nodes x 4 GH200: 16 policy GPUs (`policy_num_nodes` 4) plus 4 inference
  engines at TP2. `micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu` and `micro_forward_batch_size_per_gpu` are both 1.
- **[CHANGED by owner 2026-08-28]** d3 and d4 run at 8 nodes: the same 16 policy GPUs plus 8
  inference engines at TP2, with `n_concurrent_trials` doubled (d3 256, d4 600) and
  `num_parallel_generation_workers` 512. d2 and d5 keep the 6-node geometry. Throughput is not
  comparable across the change boundary (d3 resumes from step 51, d4 from step 33).
- Context budget is fixed at `request_window_tokens` 32768 / `max_new_tokens_per_turn` 4096, giving
  a 28672-token input allowance. Do not override derived generator, LiteLLM, vLLM, or trainer
  length fields.
- Every arm runs the full 80 steps or two epochs, whichever comes first.
- `ckpt_interval` 3, `max_ckpts_to_keep` 2, `hf_save_interval` -1 — exports cannot materialize on
  Jupiter and every export boundary killed links in the predecessor campaign.
- `resume_mode: null` selects the launcher's AUTO discovery. A literal `latest` makes an arm's
  FIRST submission fail with `CheckpointLayoutError`.
- Every arm records its full resolved configuration. A run whose configuration cannot be
  reconstructed from the record is not admissible evidence.

## Launch

Use `artifacts/scripts/launch.sh`, which wraps `python -m hpc.launch --job_type rl` with:
`--num_nodes 6` (8 for d3/d4 via `NODES=8`, owner 2026-08-28), `--time_limit 11:59:00`,
`--max_restarts 5`,
`--experiments_dir /e/data1/datasets/playground/ot-baf`.

Jupiter-fixed rules, each of which has bitten before:

- **Never pass `--reservation`.** `reformo` is an ACCOUNT, already hardwired as
  `#SBATCH --account reformo`; passing it emits a bogus `#SBATCH --reservation=reformo` and sbatch
  rejects the job.
- **Submit from the OT-Agent repo dir with `DCFT` set**, or `universal_rl.sbatch` trips
  `FATAL: WORKDIR=... is not the OpenThoughts-Agent repo root`.
- **Launch from the `otagent` conda env**, not the RL venv — task extraction imports
  `google.cloud.storage`.
- Jupiter is SLURM, not Kueue. There is no `--priority interactive` band here; the
  interactive-priority rule applies to CoreWeave/Iris only.
- Stagger multi-node launches by at least six minutes; simultaneous Hugging Face pulls have
  produced 429 rate-limit deaths.
- Confirm the SIF the rendered sbatch actually used (`experiments/<job>/sbatch/*.sbatch`). Read it;
  do not assume which runtime the launcher picked.

## Platform risk **[CHANGED — new section]**

Arms run on the **r5 / NCCL 2.28.9 container** (`skyrl_megatron_vllm0202rc0_r5.sif` with the
`skyrl_titan_overlay.img` overlay and the `sif_pydeps_titan_a1fdd7e:sif_pydeps` prefix) — the
container the TaskTrove campaign actually ran on. Owner instruction 2026-08-20.

That container carries a **known intermittent wedge**: one rank stops making progress inside an
already-initialized communicator (proxy-op pool deadlock in `ncclLocalOpAppend`), every other rank
blocks, and the watchdog kills the job. Observed at ~7 h and ~11 h of training in the closed
`jupiter-bug-trace` campaign, whose STATE.md holds the full diagnosis. **The owner has accepted this
as a cost of making research progress. Do not chase it from this campaign.**

The cu130 / NCCL 2.31.2 image is not the alternative: it hangs the policy-to-engine weight-sync
communicator init before training step 1. Do not repoint at it.

Operating consequences:

- Expect to lose a link roughly every 7–11 training hours. `--max_restarts 5` chains absorb it and
  `resume_mode` AUTO discovery picks up the latest checkpoint, so at `ckpt_interval` 3 a wedge costs
  at most three steps of work.
- A link that dies at or near walltime with no banked step is a suspected wedge. Record it in
  `STATE.md` as a platform loss and move on. It is **not** a training result and does not bear on
  any objective or dataset conclusion.
- If the chain is exhausted by wedges, relaunch it. Do not redesign the arm around the wedge.

## Maintenance authority **[CHANGED — new section]**

**Owner authorization, 2026-08-20: "Fix any issues that arise when you intermittently check in on
the experiment via your cron."** This grants the supervisor role, scoped to this campaign, authority
to diagnose and repair issues found during a sweep without asking first:

- Edit this campaign's configs and launch scripts under `artifacts/`, and the mirrored copies under
  `/e/scratch/jureap59/feuer1/jupiter-tasktrove-dapo/`.
- Cancel a failed or misconfigured chain and relaunch a corrected one.
- Apply minimal compatibility fixes to the shared SkyRL checkout at
  `/e/scratch/jureap59/feuer1/OpenThoughts-Agent/SkyRL` when a link dies on an import, API, or ABI
  error. Smallest change that unblocks; never a wholesale upgrade; never a container rebuild.

Every change records file, diff summary, and reason in `STATE.md`. The authority does **not** extend
to: stopping a healthy run, changing the swept variable or any declared invariant in this POLICY,
chasing the platform wedge, rebuilding a container, or touching anything outside this campaign and
the shared checkout. Those still need the owner.

## Health and stop rules

- The learning-signal test is `loss/avg_raw_advantages_abs` together with `raw_grad_norm`. Stop
  when advantages are repeatedly at or near zero **and** `raw_grad_norm` decays.
- Entropy at 3x its step-1 value is a watch condition; at 10x, select a checkpoint and stop.
- An entropy stop rule cannot fire on a run that has stopped learning. Pair every entropy rule
  with a liveness check on banked-step cadence.
- Do not stop on cap-pinning, falling reward, length drift, or narrowing output-length ratios
  while the learning signal is healthy.
- Capture evidence that disappears at termination before any stop.
- **Stop a misconfigured job in this series without asking** (carried from the predecessor's
  owner authorization, 2026-08-16, and scoped to this series). It applies only to a job whose
  failure cause is already diagnosed and whose corrected replacement is prepared. It does not
  apply to a healthy run, to a failure that is not yet understood, or to shared infrastructure.
  Record every stop and its reason in `STATE.md`.

## Measurement rules

- Training reward is the online health metric. The reported per-arm result is EMA-5 of
  `reward/avg_pass_at_8` through the exported checkpoint, alpha 1/3, initialized at the first
  recorded step, excluding every step after the checkpoint.
- Report a pooled-rollout proxy 95% confidence interval with every EMA-5 value, using
  `n_t = 8 x task_groups_t`. This is an intentionally optimistic precision proxy: it assumes
  rollouts supply independent aggregate evidence and does not model heterogeneous task difficulty.
- Compare arms with a 95% confidence interval on the pairwise difference. Overlap between two
  marginal intervals is not the decision rule.
- Never use step-1 reward as a baseline for a training claim; it is a difficulty probe only.
- Absolute rewards are **not** comparable with the TaskTrove predecessor campaign — different
  dataset and different objective. Do not import its difficulty band.
- Task ordering is not a confound; the train loader shuffles with the trainer seed.

# Job Summary: d=2560 MoE on 10T tokens

Big-batch d=2560 MoE training run on ~10T tokens (~1.2e23 FLOPs), with the May Recipe baked in. Below are sections on model, optimizer, training, scaling principles, and outputs.

## 1. Model

### Hyperparameters

- **hidden_dim**: 2560
- **num_layers**: 26 (heuristic-derived: `round(2560 / (64 + 4·log2(2560) − 9))`)
- **num_heads**: 20 (`hidden_dim / 128`)
- **num_kv_heads**: 5 (GQA 4:1; largest divisor of 20 ≤ 5)
- **head_dim**: 128
- **intermediate_dim**: 1280 (`ceil(d/2/128)·128`)
- **shared_expert_intermediate_dim**: 2560 (= d)
- **num_experts**: 256
- **num_experts_per_token**: 4
- **vocab_size**: 128,256
- **max_seq_len**: 4096
- **sliding_window**: 4096
- **active_params**: 2.34B (2.01B core + 0.33B lm_head; excludes embed per guidelines)
- **total_params**: 67.1B (66.4B core + 0.33B embed + 0.33B lm_head)

### Features

- **GQA**: 4:1 ratio (20 Q heads, 5 KV heads).
- **QB Routing**: stop-gradient bias updated each step from previous step's QB-β statistics (applied inside JIT).
- **Sigmoid Combine Weights**: sigmoid on unbiased router logits for selected experts.
- **GatedNorm**: rank-128 low-rank gating after RMSNorm, pre-attention and pre-MLP.
- **XSA**: subtracts V-parallel component from attention output per head.
- **Attention Gate**: learned per-head sigmoid gate on attention output, initialized to zero.
- **Shared Expert**: dense FFN (d=2560) in parallel with routed experts per layer.
- **Sliding Window**: every 4th layer (plus last) uses full window (4096); others use half (2048).
- **Half-RoPE on every layer**: RoPE applied only to the first half of Q/K per head (`q[..., :head_dim/2]`, `k[..., :head_dim/2]`). The second half is rope-free on every layer.
- **PKO (Partial Key Offset)**: on every-4th + last layer (7 of 26 layers here), the rope-free second half of K is additionally shifted by 1 position with doc-start zeroing.
- **QK Gain**: `qk_mult = 1.3`.
- **Split w_gate / w_up**: separate weight matrices for SwiGLU gate and up projections (`split_w_gate_up=True`).
- **Routing renorm sum**: 2.5 (combined-feature baseline).
- **Router z-loss**: disabled (`router_z_loss_coef = 0`).
- **Expert dispatch**: ring (May Recipe default; `moe_implementation` not exposed in current model config).

## 2. Optimizer

### Hyperparameters

(Using the refit `MoeAdamHHeuristic` from #5951.)

- **adam_lr**: 0.000432  (= `0.06602 · 1e13^-0.395 · 2560^-0.150 · √(2048·4096)`)
- **muonh_lr (= adamh_lr)**: 0.001870  (= adam_lr · 13/3)
- **beta1**: 0.9062
- **beta2**: 0.95 (clamped; `0.999^(2048/32) = 0.938` → clipped up to 0.95)
- **epsilon**: 1.06e−14  (= `1e-15 · √((32·1e13)/(2048·1.4e9))`)
- **weight_decay**: 0
- **max_grad_norm**: None (1pct-noclip schedule)
- **warmup**: 1% (= 11,921 steps)
- **decay**: None (linear schedule decays to 0 over full run)
- **min_lr_ratio**: 0.0
- **lr_schedule**: linear
- **z_loss_weight**: 0.0

### Features

- **MuonH** (`GrugMoeMuonHConfig`): scale-invariant Newton-Schulz updates on the `muonh` group (matmuls + GatedNorms), Frobenius hyperball step on top. Used in place of AdamH on weight matrices.
- **Multi-group optimizer**: 3 groups —
  - `muonh`: attn matmuls, MoE expert matmuls (gate/up/down), shared expert, GatedNorms.
  - `adamh`: lm_head / output_proj (LR = `muonh_lr`).
  - `adam`: token_embed, router weight + bias, attn_gate, 1-D norm weights (LR = `adam_lr`).

## 3. Training

- **hardware**: v4-1024 us-central2 (= 512 chips).
- **num_train_steps**: 1,192,093  (= `1e13 / (2048 · 4096)`)
- **batch_size**: 2,048 sequences
- **seq_len**: 4,096
- **tokens_per_batch**: 8.39M (= `2048 · 4096`)
- **total_tokens**: 1.00e13 (= 10T)
- **compute_budget**: ~1.21e23 FLOPs (= `6 · 2.01e9 · 1e13`)
- **mixed_precision**: `params=float32, compute=bfloat16, output=bfloat16`
- **expert_parallelism**: 4
- **data**: Nemotron mix (block-shuffled) with default validation sets
- **checkpoints**: every 10 minutes (rolling temporary), permanent every 5,000 steps

## 4. Scaling Principles

All optimizer hyperparameters derived from the refit MuonH May Recipe heuristic (issue #5951, R² = 0.996 on 17 cells).

### Learning rates (current heuristic)

- **adam_lr** = `0.06602 · tokens^-0.395 · dim^-0.150 · √(B·seq_len)`, capped at 0.05.
- **muonh_lr** = `(13/3) · adam_lr`.

### Momentum and precision

- **beta1** = 0.9062 (fixed)
- **beta2** = `clip(0.999^(B/32), 0.95, 0.9999)` → 0.95 at B=2048
- **epsilon** = `1e-15 · √((32·T) / (B·1.4e9))`

### Architecture scaling

- **num_layers** = `round(hidden_dim / (64 + 4·log2(hidden_dim) − 9))` → 26 for d=2560
- **num_heads** = `hidden_dim / 128`
- **num_kv_heads** = 4:1 GQA, largest divisor of num_heads ≤ num_heads/4
- **intermediate_dim** = `ceil(hidden_dim / 2 / 128) · 128`
- **shared_expert_intermediate_dim** = hidden_dim
- **initializer_std** = `0.5 / sqrt(hidden_dim)` ≈ 0.00988
- **num_experts** = 256, **num_experts_per_token** = 4 (fixed for May Recipe; differs from the 64-expert v16 baseline used in the 1e23 summary)

### Schedule

- **warmup** = 1% of training (1pct-noclip baseline)
- **decay** = linear all the way to 0 (no separate decay phase)
- **max_grad_norm** = None (no clipping)

## 5. Outputs

- **GCS checkpoint path**: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug/moe_may_d2560_10T/marin-big-run-moe_may_d2560_10T-XXXXXX/checkpoints` (pending — actual hash assigned at submission)
- **WandB run link**: `https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/marin-big-run-moe_may_d2560_10T` (pending)
- **Final eval metrics**: pending (run not submitted yet)
  - eval/paloma/c4_en/bpb
  - eval/paloma/macro_loss
  - eval/uncheatable_eval/macro_loss
- **Throughput** (mean over last 100 logged steps): pending

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: David's idea to use Replica sharding brings it down from 55 days to 45 days. All v4-2048 runs require 2x batch size to get good MFU, up from 33 million to 67 million. However on further testing, 67 million batch size is not training stably, compared to 33 million batch size. https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Batch-Size-Testing-67B-A2B-MoE-on-10T-tokens--VmlldzoxNzM1MTA2OQ As is standard, we scale learning rate with batch_size^0.5. This assumes that you get a less noisy gradient estimate as you scale up batch size, which typically occurs up until the critical batch size, at which point there are diminishing gains. In a prior [Issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4432) I estimated the critical batch size for compute optimal runs on our prior (similar) architecture. At compute optimal, the critical batch size is much smaller for our model size, estimated to be roughly 6-10M tokens, after which we get reduced performance. However since we are heavily overtraining, a larger batch size can be justified, since when we get to lower loss regime a larger batch size will be helpful. Many works calculate critical batch size as a function of the token budget. 22.91 · T^0.47 for 10 trillion tokens gives 29.5 million tokens, fit on AdamW. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.13738. Indications here that critical batch size is higher for Muon compared to Adam: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/1565. Llama 3 report: 3.4.1 Initial Pre-Training We pre-train Llama 3 405B using AdamW with a peak learning rate of 8 × 10−5, a linear warm up of 8,000 steps, and a cosine learning rate schedule decaying to 8 × 10−7 over 1,200,000 steps. We use a lower batch size early in training to improve training stability, and increase it subsequently to improve efficiency. Specifically, we use an initial batch size of 4M tokens and sequences of length 4,096, and double these values to a batch size of 8M sequences of 8,192 tokens after pre-training 252M tokens. We double the batch size again to 16M after pre-training on 2.87T tokens. We found this training recipe to be very stable: we observed few loss spikes and did not require interventions to correct for model training divergence. The key line here is "We use a lower batch size early in training to improve training stability". Training run references: -Arcee trained Trinity nano and mini on 10T tokens pretrain, with batch size 16 million. Then doubled to 32 million midway. -Nemotron 3 Super used 25 million batch size on 25T tokens. Given our atypical hardware setup (1024 tpu chips on a v4-2048) and smaller model size (2B active), batch size is a very high priority axis for achieving MFU, so we want to push batch size as high as possible. (of course there is some theoretical limit where we shift from diminishing gains to near zero gains). It is plausible that we could achieve a stable run start by increasing the warmup percentage from 1pct to 10pct. However, given the literature above, and the fact that we already have evidence that 33 million batch size can perform a stable warmup, it seems more sensible to start the run at 33 million at reduced MFU. If we were to keep the run at 33 million tokens per batch for the full run, we will get 63 days to complete. If we did the full run at 67 million tokens per batch, we will get 45 days to complete. Depending on if/when we shift the batch size, will determine where between 63 days and 45 days the run falls.

comments.body: (This dynamic is how understood but leaving this comment for historical accuracy) Not yet understood dynamic where numerical stability seems to suffer at full node count. Here we do a test on a very small d512 model for 200 steps (with an extremely agressive batch size). On v5p-8 it trains as expected. On v4-2048 it diverges with EP=2, or replica in (2, 16, 1024). If I move to full fp32 on output and compute, as opposed to bfloat16, it not longer diverges, but still performs substantially worse than vp5-8. This confirms that we see numerical gaps, even at fp32. Here we can see that the 33 million tokens per batch on v4-2048 is training stably, but its loss curve is a bit worse than we were getting on v4-1024. The only hardware dependent calc outside numerical precision I am aware of is the local sorting for QB. The difference in trajectory is visible in the first 10 steps, where QB has no impact. This was validated by running a full global sort version of QB and seeing it still follow the v4-2048 trajectory.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: The root cause of the issue is that the sharded NS calc in Muon was silently dropping when num_matrices didn't evenly divide into num_chips. This was originally written on v4-1024 where 256*26 is divisible by 512 chips. However it isn't divisible by 1024 chips. The fix was to explicitly replicate the NS calc over the same size as the replica axis, and also patch the silent failure. After doing this, we get stable replication of the v5p-8 d512 200 step run: Increasing precision to fp32 was helping the non orthogonalized approach not diverge, but not addressing the root cause. Lack of orthogonalization explains why the loss curve started better and then got worse over time, similar to how adam can beat muon in first couple steps. Given this knowledge, it is likely that the instability at 67 million token batch size is only due to failing to orthogonalize the gradient. So, we likely could do the full run at 67 million token batch size. However, starting at 33 million batch size for the first 5% of the run will likely be more token efficient, and only add 1 day of runtime. (46 day total). This also lets us validate the full warmup curve against the v4-1024 warmup curve which ran at 33 million batch size. Reflecting on the bug: 1. Transitioning from small scale tests to prod scale implementation will always require iterating on the code. (lax.scan to fit in memory, iterating on the sharding implementation). 2. This introduces risk of incorrect implementation. In particular due to perception of time pressure of having the hardware sit idle. 3. This incorrectness can be subtely incorrect in ML world. (though in this particular case this issue should have errored loudly, but I did not review this agent written resharding close enough) For future runs, recommend we have: 1. Small scale code should have prior code review and be checked into main. 2. After we get large scale code implemented, we should raise PR and get human review on the (ideally minor) changes to get small scale code working at prod scale. 3. Always replicate a small scale run on the prod hardware. (this has now been done for this run) 4. Have a script that runs series of validation checks against the first 200 steps of wandb logs. (checking all param inits, param norms over initial training with hyperball, routing entropy, activity across all layers, train stability, etc). These always get eye-balled but the level of rigor is not the same.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: Preregistered loss target for stage 1 of the run (first 8T tokens): 2.269 paloma macro loss when evaled at seqlen 8192 on 1024 sequences per eval. This projection is viewed as our best estimate, but there are a large number of assumptions underpinning it: 1. Assuming an irreducible loss of 1.4. Prior large scale runs at seqlen 4k have indicated an irreducible loss of 1.5. Extending the seqlen to 8k should slightly reduce this, by reducing the number of evals that start a sequence mid-context. 2. The smaller scale runs had no logit z loss. After observing large grad norm on the d1024 run, I did a follow up experiment re-adding z loss to the final logit, which helped control the gradient and gave better evals and train loss. https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Z-Loss-Under-OverTrain-650B-tokens---VmlldzoxNzMyODk1NQ. 3. We are heavily increasing the batch size for the 10T run, which will increase the final loss. I am assuming that point 2 will roughly cancel out with this. 4. We are extrapolating from 3 points- our prior 1e23 run extrapolated at compute optimal from over 20 points. In particular, runs at d512 seem to extrapolate worse due to heavier parameter skew in lm_head due to high vocab size of 128k. We chose to not extrapolate from more points to enable the 10T run to start sooner. 5. We will be at 24% peak LR at the end of stage 1. Predicting model performance before full LR cooldown may have different dynamics as we scale. Given these assumptions, I anticipate we will be able to use the actual achieved loss to update our knowledge of training dynamics and which assumptions to revisit.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 Job summary for the d=2560 67B / 2B-active MoE 10T pretrain

# Job Summary: 67B / 2B-active MoE 10T pretrain (d=2560, MuonH, v4-2048)

~10.07T-token MuonH MoE pretrain at d=2560 / 67B total params / 2.01B active per token (run_id `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep16_bs4096_seq8192_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_10T`; batch ramp from 4,096 → 8,192 at step 15,000, with total steps reduced so total tokens stay near 10T). Below are sections on model, optimizer, training, and scaling principles.

## 1. Model

### Hyperparameters

- **hidden_dim**: 2560
- **num_layers**: 26
- **num_heads**: 20
- **num_kv_heads**: 5 (GQA 4:1)
- **head_dim**: 128
- **intermediate_dim**: 1280 (MoE expert FFN; `ceil(hidden_dim / 2 / 128) * 128`)
- **shared_expert_intermediate_dim**: 2560 (= hidden_dim)
- **num_experts**: 256
- **num_experts_per_token**: 4
- **vocab_size**: 128,256
- **max_seq_len**: 8,192
- **sliding_window**: 2,048
- **total_params**: 67.1B
- **active_params**: 2.01B per token (2.34B w/ lm_head)

### Features

- **GQA**: 4:1 ratio (20 Q heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128)
- **QB Routing**: stop-gradient bias updated each step from previous step's QB-β statistics (applied inside JIT)
- **Sigmoid Combine Weights**: sigmoid on unbiased router logits for the K=4 selected experts (not softmax). Combine weights are then renormalized to sum to **2.5** across the K selected experts (`_ROUTING_RENORM_SUM = 2.5` in `model.py:51`), which effectively rescales the routed-expert contribution per token by 2.5× compared to a standard sum-to-1 (softmax-style) normalization.
- **GatedNorm**: rank-128 low-rank gating after RMSNorm, pre-attention and pre-MLP
- **Shared Expert**: dense FFN (d=2560) in parallel with routed experts per layer
- **Sliding Window**: every 4th layer + final layer uses full window (8,192); the other 19 layers use the short window (2,048). Layout: 7 long / 19 short (`i % 4 == 3 or i == num_layers - 1`).
- **disable_long_rope**: long (full-attention) layers skip rotary embedding entirely. Short (windowed) layers still apply half-RoPE.
- **disable_pko**: no per-key offset on long layers. Plain attention only.
- **RoPE**: partial rotary — only half of `head_dim` is rotated (the leading 64 of 128 dims), the rest is passed through unchanged. Applied on short (windowed) layers only; long (full-attention) layers skip RoPE entirely per `disable_long_rope`.
- **ArrayStacked + scan**: all 26 blocks stacked via `jax.lax.scan` (`use_array_stacked_blocks=True`) for reduced compile time and HBM footprint

## 2. Optimizer

### Hyperparameters

- **muonh_lr**: 0.003733 → **0.005279** at step 15,000 (×√2 with the BS doubling)
- **adam_lr**: 0.000861 → **0.001218** at step 15,000 (= muonh_lr / (13/3); also ×√2)
- **beta1**: 0.9062 (unchanged across the BS ramp)
- **beta2**: 0.95 — clamped both before and after the ramp (raw formula 0.999^(B*S/131072) gives 0.774 pre-ramp and 0.599 post-ramp; both clamp to 0.95)
- **epsilon**: ~8.01 × 10⁻¹⁹ → **~5.66 × 10⁻¹⁹** at step 15,000 (÷√2 with the BS doubling)
- **weight_decay**: 0
- **max_grad_norm**: None (no clipping in MuonH 1pct-noclip schedule)
- **warmup**: 0.01 (1% of training; ~3,000 steps)
- **decay**: None (linear decay over the whole post-warmup period)
- **min_lr_ratio**: 0.05 (decay to 5% of peak by end-of-training)
- **lr_schedule**: linear
- **z_loss_weight**: 1e-4 (logit z-loss; router z-loss = 0)

### Features

- **MuonH (Muon + Frobenius hyperball)**: Newton-Schulz orthogonalization on weight matrices followed by a scale-invariant Frobenius-hyperball projection. Three LR groups:
  - **muonh** — 2D weight matrices and stacked MoE expert weights (NS + hyperball)
  - **adamh** — `lm_head` / `output_proj`. AdamH = Adam moments + Frobenius hyperball (`scale_by_adamh`); no Newton-Schulz. Uses the same LR schedule as muonh.
  - **adam** — biases, RMSNorm scales, router weights, gated-norm scales, and (via `rmsnorm_to_adam=True`) stacked RMSNorm scales
- **Multi-group optimizer**: separate optax chains per group routed by parameter path (see `experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py:create_mask`).
- **Logit Z-Loss**: penalizes large output-logit norm to stabilize training (no router z-loss in this run).

## 3. Training

- **hardware**: v4-2048 (1,024 chips), us-central2, production priority, --no-preemptible
- **num_train_steps**: 157,500 (reduced from 300,000 to absorb the batch-size doubling and hold total tokens ~constant)
- **batch_size**: 4,096 → 8,192 sequences (step change at step 15,000 ≈ 5% of training)
- **seq_len**: 8,192
- **tokens_per_step**: 33,554,432 (~33.5M) for steps 0–14,999; 67,108,864 (~67.1M) for steps 15,000–157,499
- **total_tokens**: ~1.007 × 10¹³ (~10.07T) — 5.03 × 10¹¹ from the BS=4,096 phase (15,000 steps) + 9.56 × 10¹² from the BS=8,192 phase (142,500 steps)
- **compute_budget**: ~1.69 × 10²³ FLOPs (SWA-aware, with lm_head)
- **mixed_precision**: `params=float32,compute=bfloat16,output=bfloat16`
- **mesh**: `(replica_dcn=16, data=64, expert=1, model=1)`. EP=1, `replica_axis_size=16`. Batch is sharded across (replica_dcn, data, expert) → 1,024 shards.
- **expert_parallelism**: 1 (no expert sharding; routed experts replicated across the expert axis)
- **data**: datakit MoE mixture (`_datakit_data_config`, simulated epoching disabled) with default paloma validation sets
- **eval cadence**: every 3,000 steps; `eval_batch_size=1024`, `max_eval_batches=1` (8.39M tokens per eval)
- **checkpoints**: permanent every 3,000 steps; temp save every 60 minutes; auto-resume on preemption

## 4. Scaling Principles

All optimizer hyperparameters derived from the MuonH May Recipe refit (issue #5951, 17 finished cells across d ∈ {512, 768, 1024, 1280} × R ∈ {4, 10, 20, 60, 120, 240} × lr_mult ∈ {0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6}, R² = 0.996). Reference seq_len = 4096; conversions assume `tokens_per_batch = batch_size * seq_len`.

### Learning rates

- **muonh_lr** = `18.31 · T^(-0.395) · d^(-0.150) · sqrt(B)`, capped at 0.05
  - Equivalent to `lr_coeff · T^(-0.395) · d^(-0.150) · sqrt(tokens_per_batch)` with `lr_coeff = 0.06602` (= 18.31 / ((13/3) · 64))
  - At T = 1.007e13, d = 2560, B*S = 33.55M → **muonh_lr ≈ 0.003733**
- **adam_lr** = muonh_lr / (13/3) ≈ **0.000861**
- **adamh_lr** = muonh_lr ≈ **0.003733** (the `adamh` group — `lm_head` / `output_proj` — uses the same LR schedule as muonh, via `scale_by_adamh`: Adam moments + Frobenius hyperball, no Newton-Schulz)

### Momentum and precision

- **beta1** = 0.9062 (fixed)
- **beta2** = `clip(0.999^(tokens_per_batch / 131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`
  - At B*S = 33.55M → raw 0.999^256 ≈ 0.774 → clamped to **0.95**
- **epsilon** = `9.676e-18 · sqrt((B0 · T) / (tokens_per_batch · T0))` with B0=32, T0=1.4e9
  - At T = 1.007e13, tokens_per_batch = 33.55M → **epsilon ≈ 8.01e-19**

### Architecture scaling

- **num_layers** = `round(hidden_dim / (64 + 4·log2(hidden_dim) - 9))` = 26 for d=2560
- **num_heads** = `hidden_dim / 128` = 20
- **num_kv_heads** = largest divisor of num_heads ≤ num_heads // 4 = 5 (GQA 4:1)
- **intermediate_dim** = `ceil(hidden_dim / 2 / 128) · 128` = 1280
- **shared_expert_intermediate_dim** = hidden_dim = 2560
- **initializer_std** ≈ `0.5 / sqrt(2560)` ≈ 0.00988
- **num_experts** = 256, **num_experts_per_token** = 4 (fixed; differs from the 1e23 d=5120 run which used 64 experts)

### Schedule

- **warmup** = 1% of training (~3,000 steps)
- **decay** = none (linear schedule decays over the whole post-warmup period)
- **min_lr_ratio** = 0.05 (decay to 5% of peak)
- **lr_schedule** = linear

## 5. Outputs

- **GCS checkpoint path**: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep16_bs4096_seq8192_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_10T-<hash>/checkpoints` (pending — populated on first save)
- **WandB run link**: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep16_bs4096_seq8192_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_10T
- **iris job**: `/larry/iris-run-job-20260627-154212`
- **Final eval metrics** (pending — run in progress):
  - eval/paloma/macro_loss (projected: 2.269 @ 0.8 of training; see issue #6044)
  - eval/paloma/c4_en/bpb
  - eval/uncheatable_eval/macro_loss
- **Throughput** (pending — fill from mean over last 100 logged steps):
  - throughput/mfu
  - throughput/tokens_per_second

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
Report where run will be tracked: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/67B-A2B-MoE-on-10T-tokens--VmlldzoxNzM1OTMxMQ

Notable updates to architecture:
1. Since we are planning to extend context out to 262k, there will likely be several iterations on datamix and attention scaling to enable this. To minimize possible confounders during this process, PKO has been disabled, along with RoPE on the global layers. This puts our architecture close to published literature on effective long context extension. Once we have successfully extended context using textbook approaches, then we can consider adding back partial rope and PKO. We may be incurring a 10-20% efficiency hit from this, but the risk/reward tradeoff here of taking a controlled approach seems worthwhile to maximize learnings and our later models.
2. Re-adding final logit z loss. At compute optimal scale, z loss had a neglible impact. However on the new data mix and extreme overtrain, we see meaningful gains from including z loss, both on the train loss and evals. https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Z-Loss-Under-OverTrain-650B-tokens---VmlldzoxNzMyODk1NQ.
3. Batch size schedule. The hardware profile is heavily encouraging us to run at extremely large batch sizes to achieve acceptable MFU. Instead of performing the full run at 67 million tokens per batch, we are running the first 5 pct at half that. Which is the window when smaller batch sizes have the biggest impact.
4. LR decay to 0.05 instead of 0. This is because we will extend out from 64k->262k, and do subsequent posttrain. decay to zero is only optimal if we have no subsequent weight updates.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Final 1 T-token cooldown submitted** (third and last in the 67B-a2b 10T campaign)

- **Iris job**: `/larry/iris-run-job-20260815-212009` · [dashboard](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Flarry%2Firis-run-job-20260815-212009)
- **Launcher**: [`experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step141k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b054d8912d/experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step141k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py) on branch `june_tpu_67b_a2b`, pinned at commit [`b054d8912d`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/b054d8912d)
- **Reads from**: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs8192_seq8192_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_resume15k_v2_10T-9fcc1f/checkpoints/step-141000/` (main-run pretraining checkpoint at 9 T tokens seen; manifest written 2026-08-15 21:16 UTC, complete)
- **Wandb run**: `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step141k` (fresh — same group `june-tpu-67b-a2b-cooldown` as the two earlier cooldowns)

### Config

| Knob | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resume step | 141,000 | main run's ~9 T-token mark (89.5% of the 157,500-step horizon) |
| Cooldown steps | 15,000 | 1.007 T tokens = ~last 1 T of the 10 T campaign |
| `seq_len` / `batch_size` | 65,536 / 1,024 | 67.1 M tokens/step (unchanged from source's 8,192 × 8,192) |
| `qk_mult` | 1.57 | matches the winning all-layers YaRN `mscale(coef=0.1)` from the step-102k cooldown |
| LR | 0.000822 → 0.000264, linear | joins source at step-141k, decays to source floor over 15k steps |
| Data mix | phase-1 (mix 2) only | main run's been in mix 2 since step 127,500 |
| `resume_data_offset` | **13,824,000** samples | new field: exact-position continuation — see below |
| `hybrid_attention_flops_accounting` | True | 7 full + 19 sw=2048 layers → MFU reports ~0.44× the naive count (honest) |
| Save + eval | every 1,500 steps | 10 permanent saves + 10 evals over the cooldown |
| Iris retries | `--max-retries 100` | auto-recovery on the recurring coord-service TCP-close failure (#7430) |

### Data-position continuation (new mechanism)

Prior cooldowns (step-39k, step-102k) used a fresh mix-2 shuffle from position 0. This one continues main run's mix-2 stream *exactly*:

- Main run consumed **905.97 B mix-2 tokens** between steps 127,500 → 141,000 (13,500 steps × 8,192 seq × 8,192 BS).
- Cooldown at seq=65,536 wants to start at the same underlying token offset → sample-index **13,824,000**.
- New `resume_data_offset` field on `GrugMoeLaunchConfig2xBS` builds a 3-stage BatchSchedule `[(0, 98), (135000, 99), (141000, 1024)]` that lands `cumulative_size(141000)` at exactly 13,824,000 samples. Zero re-consumption of main run's exposure, zero skip past it.
- Per-bucket read positions in each of the 168 mix-2 buckets exactly continue where main run left off; the mixture-shuffle order differs (unavoidable: mixture-shuffle indexes are in cooldown's seq_len enumeration, which is 8× the main run's).
- 12 small-weight buckets will epoch during the 1 T cooldown budget (aggregate ~1.3% extra re-exposure; largest is `c34q4` at 2.88×).

### MFU accounting

Restored the hybrid-attention FLOPs accounting from the step-39k cooldown (originally commit 5681efbe3f, reverted for hash-continuity at the time). At seq=65,536, `lm_flops_per_token` for our 26-layer model (7 full + 19 sliding-window at sw=2048) is **9.74×10⁹** vs. the naive all-full-attention 2.22×10¹⁰ — so `throughput/mfu` will report about 2.28× lower than a naive counter for the same wall-clock work. Wandb history for the pretraining run is unchanged (naive accounting there); this only applies to the cooldown.

### Adjacent commit contents on branch `june_tpu_67b_a2b`

- [`200f995326`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/200f995326) — step-141k launcher + `resume_data_offset` extension on `GrugMoeLaunchConfig2xBS`
- [`0a2b32cd84`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/0a2b32cd84) — hybrid-attn MFU accounting (`lm_flops_per_token` sliding_window params + `GrugModelConfig.hybrid_attention_flops_accounting` flag + `override_output_path` pin on the pretraining launcher to defend against the config-hash shift)
- [`b054d8912d`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/b054d8912d) — BUILD_DATE bump for iris server floor

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up: two 262k context-extension probes from the same step-156000 checkpoint above.

## Runs

| variant | qk_mult | wandb | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| formula-scaled (`1.3 · (0.1·ln(32)+1)`) | 1.75 | [run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep1_ctx4_bs256_seq262144_ctxext_step156k) | finished |
| held from step-141k cooldown | 1.57 | [run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep1_ctx4_bs256_seq262144_ctxext_step156k_qk157) | running |

## Launchers

- qk=1.75: [`experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ctxext_step156k_seq262k_bs256_ctx4_muon.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/june_tpu_67b_a2b/experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ctxext_step156k_seq262k_bs256_ctx4_muon.py)
- qk=1.57: [`experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ctxext_step156k_seq262k_bs256_ctx4_muon_qk157.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/june_tpu_67b_a2b/experiments/grug/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ctxext_step156k_seq262k_bs256_ctx4_muon_qk157.py)

Both resume from the step-141k cooldown's `step-156000` checkpoint above.

## Design spec

- **seq_len**: 65,536 → **262,144** (4× extension).
- **BS**: 1024 → **256** sequences → tokens/step stays at 256 · 262,144 = 67.1 M (matches the step-141k cooldown's per-step token budget).
- **Steps**: 1,000 (step 156,000 → 157,000) → **67.1 B tokens** total.
- **LR**: linear decay from 5 % of source peak (0.000264, matches cooldown exit LR) → 1 % of source peak (0.0000528), no ramp. Implementation pins the resume schedule's abstract "peak" to 0.000264 with `min_lr_ratio=0.2` so the floor lands at exactly `0.000264 · 0.2 = 0.0000528`.
- **qk_mult**: 1.75 (`1.3 · (0.1·ln(32) + 1) = 1.7506`, rounded) vs. 1.57 (held from the step-141k cooldown, which used `1.3 · (0.1·ln(8) + 1) = 1.5703`). Both applied Q-only as a single logit multiplier (one-sided YaRN; note this delivers `mscale` on logits, not the paper's `mscale²`).
- **Data continuation**: exact per-token — `resume_data_offset = (13,500·8,192·8,192 + 15,000·1,024·65,536) / 262,144 = 7,296,000` samples. The launcher builds a 3-stage BS schedule `[(0, 46), (36000, 47), (156000, 256)]` that hits exactly 7,296,000 cumulative samples at step 156,000 (zero re-consumption AND zero skip). Post-run cumulative mix-2 consumption = **1.980 T tokens** (98.99% of the 2 T mix-2 design budget).
- **Checkpoints / evals**: every 250 steps (4 total: 156,250 / 156,500 / 156,750 / 157,000).
- **Mesh** on v4-2048 (1024 chips): `(replica_dcn=1, data=256, context=4, expert=1, model=1)`. `batch_shards = replica · data · expert = 256`, `per_device_parallelism = 1`. `context_axis_size = 4` shards the seq axis → `seq_per_device = 65,536` (identical chip-local seq to the step-141k cooldown, our known-good memory point).

## Context-parallel implementation

Landed on this branch as a self-contained addition; `context_axis_size = 1` is a no-op vs. the pre-CP code path.

- **Mesh axis** (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/sharding.py`): added `"context"` to `_GRUG_MESH_AXIS_NAMES`; `compact_grug_mesh` now takes `context_axis_size`. `_batch_axes()` returns the full flat-token axes and now includes `"context"` when present so MoE psums / shard_maps reduce over the correct set.
- **Grug MoE model** (`experiments/grug/moe/model.py`): seq axis on Q / residual stream / MLP / embed / output_proj sharded on `"context"` via helpers `_seq_spec_3d` / `_seq_spec_4d` / `_token_spec`. K/V explicitly resharded to seq=`None` before splash (splash's TPU entry refuses `kv_seq_shards > 1`), i.e. the **all-gather-KV** flavor of CP.
- **RoPE cache**: `_apply_half_rope` reshards its precomputed cos/sin to `P(None, "context", None, None)` so the per-shard broadcast against context-sharded Q/K lines up.
- **Segment IDs**: `Transformer.__call__` reshards q_seg to `P(_BATCH_AXES, "context")` and kv_seg to `P(_BATCH_AXES, None)` before passing the mask to splash, so splash's per-shard segment-id shape check matches.
- **Router / QB shard_map**: uses `_token_axes()` (batch + context) for the shard_map in_specs and `pmean` so the QB threshold pmean reduces across both data and context shards.
- **Splash kernel wrapping** (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py`): the splash kernel is now passed as an input to `shard_map` with its own `manual_sharding_spec` (mirroring the classical levanter path). Prior closure-capture would leave `fwd_mask_info.q_sequence` at global shape, and splash's forward broadcast would fail against the local `q_seq_len`. Each mask_info leaf is `jax.reshard`ed to the manual spec before the shard_map, since shard_map now rejects mismatched in_specs.
- **(B,S)↔(B*S) reshapes**: `_flatten_bs` / `_unflatten_bs` helpers wrap `jnp.reshape` with explicit `out_sharding` (`_token_spec()` and `_seq_spec_3d()` respectively). einops's `rearrange` goes through `array.reshape()` with no sharding hint, which JAX can't lower when two sharded axes fuse into one.
- **Trainer mesh** (`experiments/grug/moe/launch_2x_bs.py`): passes `"context": context_axis_size` into the TrainerConfig's `MeshConfig` so `data_axis_size` (used for the BS-divisibility check) reflects only the actual batch shards.
- **Loss parity** verified at `context = {1, 2, 4}` for a small config: identical loss at c=2, bf16-precision noise (~1e-6) at c=4.

## Status

- qk=1.75 finished all 1000 steps. Train loss dropped 1.325 → **1.159** across the extension; paloma macro-loss 2.177 → **2.208** (small uptick from a fresh eval at the new seq/temperature; c4_en, dolma, m2d2, redpajama all continue improving during the 1000 steps).
- qk=1.57 in flight, tracking qk=1.75 closely so far.
- Known artifact: `wikitext_103` and `ptb` paloma tags read `0.0` in both runs. Root cause: `TokenSeqDataset.async_len = total_tokens // seq_len` uses integer division, so any val cache smaller than one 262k window (wikitext_103 ~247k tokens, ptb ~86k tokens) yields **0** eval sequences. Not a training bug; only affects small paloma tags at long seq_len.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
Recommendation:
Run multiple experiments, varying the following factors:
- qk_mult. This specifies the attention 'sharpness' (how strongly can it natively pick out a single target). It started at 1.3 during 8k seqlen, then was bumped to 1.57 during 65k seqlen. This is a softer version of yarn mscale. For 262k, could hold at 1.57, or bump to ~1.75 or 2. Increasing may help on longer documents and slightly hurt on shorter documents. Previously tried an experiment bumping it only on global layers, didn't help. (However may be worth it on this 65k->262k extension)
- number of steps. Defaulting to 1k. 67B tokens. Can be varied.
- LR schedule. Defaulting to linear decay from 5 pct peak to 1 pct peak.
- Checkpoint averaging. Am saving checkpoints every 250 steps during this cooldown. EMA over these may give stronger final model.
- Data. First two experiments were on the exact same mix2 from this run, continuing off from where last step was. Alternatively, can upweight long context data (data over 65k seqlen). Or, swap to datamix we are using on the 535B hero run.

Checkpoints exist for the two tests above, both they don't have a long context eval in wandb. This will be good to be comparing against. Need to debug and fix the 0 eval score for the evals with under 262k context length.

issues.body:
Issue is to describe the Hero Run scaling ladder, config, and track its performance.

Tracking: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng

Details on the full model spec is in the comment below.

### Why run a scaling ladder?

1. This lets us project the model performance and compare it to the scaling projections of our prior recipes. If our projection looks meaningfully worse, then we know we need to go back to the drawing board on some aspect of the model or data. This step can catch a lot of bugs!
2. We can look at how training dynamics change as we scale, in particular the gradient norms and token dropping. In our last run, the scaling ladder caught gradient norm growth to over 4 as we scaled out token horizon, which caused us to find a fix with logit z loss. Later ablations showed that without this fix, runs under certain conditions like high batch size would completely blow up mid-run.
3. We can project our evals across the entire trajectory of the run. This means that across the entire ~100 day run, we know exactly how we are doing compared to the projection. If at any point we fail to match the projection, it can prompt early investigation into training dynamics.
4. If something strange start to happen in the Hero run, we can reference the smaller scales runs to see if its actually normal. For instance, in prior scaling ladders we saw the grad norm grow heavily up to 40% of the run, then decrease as the LR decays. When we saw this on the hero run, having the small scale reference gave us confidence we didn't need to intervene, as long as the gradient followed the same pattern (steady growth for 40% of run).
5. It only costs 1% of total compute.
### What is our EP hardware implementation?
Described in detail here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html.
We are hand-rolling our own EP implementation, props to @ravwojdyla, since we have not found a more performant variant on JAX XLA on GPU. 

### What is our long context extension plan?
Our last run was 8k seqlen pretrain, followed by 65k extension for 1T tokens, followed by 262k extension (to occur end of Aug). Prior to that run we have used 4k seqlen pretrain. For this run we are going back to 4k seqlen pretrain to start, to enable better expert balancing (twice as many sequences per batch). We wanted to minimize risk here because our EP token dropping implementation is more experimental. (our last run was dropless FSDP). Prior tests showed token dropping grow from ~7% to ~40% when extending from 4k to 65k seqlen. Our new pooled/wave EP drops about half as many tokens (3%) at 4k seqlen; however the token dropping is likely still excessively high at 65k seqlen.

We will spend 1-2 days to do an early cooldown at roughly 10-20 days into the run, to enable RL experiments, which will be our first full scale data point at how longer context influences dropping. A nice property of this test is that the cooldown will not contaminate or impact the main run, so we have some flexibility to collect data on how an extension approach impacts dropping. Our options will be:
1. If we have landed a Jax Mixture of Kittens or dropless ragged all-to-all, then we can swap to that for the cooldown. Prior small scale tests showed the model was robust from swapping from small amounts of dropping (5%) to dropless mid-run.
2. Otherwise, we can increase our capacity factor, and accept some amount of dropping.
3. If we find that neither of these options are suitable, the next option would be to introduce sequence level balancing mid-run (though forcing the experts to re-specialize mid-run will likely be worse than accepting some amount of dropping). 

Extending context will involve updating qk_mult according to mscale=X⋅ln(new_seqlen/old_seqlen)+1, testing coefficients near 0.1 (can quickly eval a range during extension on 1 rack). If the data from the first cooldown looks smooth, will plan on 4k->8k at 50 pct into run, then 8k->65k at about 95 pct, then a targeted 262k phase near end, based on data we collect from taking the 67B-A2B from 65k to 262k.

Have further derisked token dropping by staying at 2 shared experts, each at half width. 8 active experts are also at half width. However due to latent MoE 2x compression on active experts, we are effectively running at hidden_dim width neurons shared, and 2x hidden_dim neurons routed. Having 1/3 of our neurons come from shared expert will provide a stronger backbone in the event of high dropping. We see learning still progress with zero loss spikes even at 40 pct dropping.

### What if we see delays, beyond our buffer (hardware failure, MFU degradation)?
Up to roughly 25% of the token budget, the default approach will be to compensate by decreasing the token horizon of the run. Since we are using linear LR decay, we would update the decay rate to still reach 0.05 peak at whatever the new horizon point is, and update the datamix.
